title: BlackRock’s ‘Widow Maker’ Treasury ETF Slides to 2004 Low
summary: The rout in longer-dated US Treasuries has sent a popular BlackRock Inc. exchange-traded fund tumbling to its lowest level in over two decades, as concerns around sticky inflation continue battering fixed-income portfolios.

title: Trucking Stocks Fall on Legal Risk in Worst Month Since Tariffs
summary: Trucking and logistics stocks are poised for their worst month in more than a year, weighed down by mounting concerns over a recent legal decision that can hurt industry brokers, alongside disappointing earnings.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 31
summary: Oil posted its biggest monthly gain since March as traders grappled with simmering global conflicts and threats to supply from the Persian Gulf to the Black Sea.

title: Couche-Tard CEO Expects Żabka Investor Pressure to Raise Bid
summary: The head of Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. said he expects pushback from some Żabka Group SA shareholders on the Canadian company’s $8.7 billion takeover offer, but is still confident about getting the deal done.

title: Tech Stocks Power Wall Street Gains at End of July: Markets Wrap
summary: A rally in several technology heavyweights lifted stocks in the final stretch of a dizzying July as strong earnings overshadowed inflation worries that have rattled the bond market.

title: Colombia to Build Up Reserves as Peso Strengthens to 7-Year High
summary: Colombia launched a program to accumulate as much $4 billion in international reserves, moving to weaken the nation’s currency from a seven-year high.

title: Trump Casts Doubt on New Iran Negotiations as War Drags On
summary: Retired Army General Wesley Clark, who served as Supreme Allied Commander Europe, said the more the US wants negotiations, the stronger the hand Iran thinks it has at the table. Clark said that the Iranian government sees the fight against the US as existential and that it will take more than taking out a few oil refineries to get the IRGC to surrender, particularly as they receive more backing from Russia and China.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Future of the Democratic Party Runs Through Michigan
summary:
On today’s Big Take podcast, host David Gura sits down with senior political correspondent Nancy Cook and Bloomberg Opinions’ Ronald Brownstein to unpack the stakes of the Michigan Democratic primary, where a centrist candidate is facing off against a Democratic-Socialist-backed progressive — and what their showdown could reveal about the party’s future.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fed Needs Clear Inflation Target and Messaging, Clarida Says
summary: Former Federal Reserve Vice Chairman Richard Clarida joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money" to discuss this week's Fed decision, Chairman Kevin Warsh's communication decisions and the increased divergence in the K-shaped economy. Clarida is currently a global economic adviser for Pimco. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Very Positive on European Stocks: UBS’s Panseri
summary: UBS Wealth Management France CIO Claudio Panseri discusses European earnings, how Europe works with AI stocks, and gives her outlook on bond yields. She speaks with Anna Edwards and Guy Johnson on ‘Opening Trade.’ (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Says Not Involved in Redirecting Pakistan-Bound LNG Tanker
summary: The US said it had no role in redirecting the first Qatari liquefied natural gas shipment to transit the Strait of Hormuz in more than three weeks.

title: Russia’s Cheap, Upgraded Cruise Missiles Pound Black Sea Ports
summary: Ukraine’s Black Sea ports are being ravaged by a new type of Russian missile, the Banderol — whose defining feature is its low cost.

title: CreditSights’ Winnie Cisar Gives Outlook on Tech Bonds
summary: CreditSights Global head of credit strategy Winnie Cisar discusses the tech space and expectations for credit markets and borrowing. She speaks on “Bloomberg Real Yield” on July 30, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Stocks Rally to End a Turbulent Month; Amazon Jumps 15%
summary: US stocks rose on Friday, erasing earlier losses, as Amazon.com Inc.’s 15% rally after stellar results lifted a broad sweep of companies benefiting from zeal for artificial intelligence.

title: Exxon, Chevron Steer Windfall Profits Into Paying Down Debt
summary: ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. and Chevron Corp. plowed blowout profits into debt reduction rather than huge buyback increases in a sign of Big Oil’s caution about how long war-driven price rallies will last.

title: Gold Dips as Traders Eye Dollar Recovery Against Yen, Fed Path
summary: Gold fell as an intervention-driven rally in the yen stalled, helping the dollar snap a five-day run of losses.

title: Jane Street-Backed Exchange Sells Control to TMX Group
summary: MEMX LLC, an exchange operator backed by Jane Street and Morgan Stanley, will combine with equity options market BOX in a deal that gives control of the merged entity to Canada’s leading stock exchange group.

title: Big Tech’s AI Divide Widens | Open Interest 7/31/2026
summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." The Big Tech divide widens as Amazon’s AI bet delivers, while chip shortages pressure Apple. John Blackledge breaks down AWS demand and Amazon’s trillion-dollar cloud potential. Will Power explains why Apple’s strong demand may outweigh supply turbulence. Plus, Citadel’s latest AI deal, improving consumer sentiment, and the market risks heading into August. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Odd Lots: Why Private Credit Got Entangled With Insurance
summary:
Insurers have quietly become a major driver of the private credit boom, changing the insurance industry itself and raising a number of questions about risk and regulation.

Andrew Granato and Pranjal Drall, authors of a new paper, “Private Credit's State Backstop: How Private Equity Socializes Risk Through Insurers," tell Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal how both sides benefit from the partnership and why taxpayers might ultimately be on the hook. (Source: Bloomberg)
